title: Q and A on DAP decision (2)
primary_topics: DAP Q&A part 2 July 27, 2014 -- continuation of A405 July 20 nine-question total series (Q6-Q9 here, Q1-Q5 in A405)

Q6: Fellow-augmentation-officials applicability -- Senate president + House speaker + CJ + ConCom heads also enjoy power of augmentation, may exercise it provided constitutional limitations observed (DAP not declared unconstitutional)

Constitutional and Fiscal Autonomy Group (CFAG) routine-augmentation history: judiciary + Office of Ombudsman + Comelec + COA + CSC routinely used augmentation to realign savings from vacant positions to increase compensation and fringe benefits
Q7-Q8: OSG MR documented-claims of TWO SC cross-border augmentation 'acts and practices' that didn't observe DAP-decision limitations

First SC act: July 17, 2012 (Justice Antonio T. Carpio as acting CJ during interregnum between Corona May 28 2012 Senate-ouster and Sereno Aug 24 2012 appointment) -- Court 'earmarked its existing savings of P1.865 billion to augment the P100 million budget for the Manila Hall of Justice' (item in 2012 DOJ-OSec budget under Executive Department), a 'cross-border augmentation'

Second SC act: March 5, 2013 (Sereno already CJ) -- Court resolution 'requested the DBM to transfer the P100 million in the budget of the DOJ for the Manila Hall of Justice to the Judiciary... to fund the construction of the Malabon Hall of Justice... which has no item in the 2012 or the 2013 GAA'
Sereno Dec 23, 2013 withdrawal-letter to DBM after DAP petitions filed and being heard -- withdrew the realignment request
OSG's 'benign and necessary interdepartmental augmentations' theory framing; cross-border-transfers 'not begun by President Aquino' but used by Ramos + Estrada + GMA also

Q9: CJP-as-retired-CJ commentary -- OSG did not denounce SC acts as unconstitutional, merely observed practices 'based on understanding of the constitutional provision that coincides with the government's'; SC said it 'will justify these two acts' in MR resolution; CJP won't preempt that justification

CJP's three closing points: (1) two SC acts reinforce operative-fact-doctrine application; (2) strengthen Q3 (last Sunday's A405) call to delete or clarify 'alien' p.90 obiter-dictum on authors/proponents/implementors; (3) affirm power of augmentation 'is quite difficult to understand even by the most astute legal minds... not taught in law schools, not explained in standard political law textbooks'
sub_topics: This is continuation of questions raised on SC decision on Disbursement Acceleration Program or DAP taken up in this space last Sunday (A405)

Q6: In Question No. 5 a week ago, CJP said PNoy can use DAP again in future provided he observes constitutional limitations -- can Senate president, House speaker, CJ, and heads of independent constitutional commissions do the same?
Answer: Yes, same power of augmentation (DAP's sophisticated name) is granted by Constitution to aforesaid officials
They may continue exercising such power (not struck down as unconstitutional by SC) provided they, like President, observe limitations in decision
In past, Constitutional and Fiscal Autonomy Group (CFAG), composed of judiciary + Office of Ombudsman + Comelec + COA + CSC, routinely used power of augmentation
To realign savings from vacant positions to increase compensation and fringe benefits of incumbent officials and personnel
Q7: Please explain PNoy's claim, in OSG-filed MR, that SC has committed TWO 'acts and practices' that did not observe the limitations set out in the decision

OSG said that on July 17, 2012, when Justice Antonio T. Carpio was acting CJ (during interregnum after CJ Renato C. Corona was ousted and disqualified from holding any public office by Senate per its 'Judgment' dated May 28, 2012, and appointment of new CJ Maria Lourdes P. A. Sereno on Aug 24, 2012)

Court 'earmarked its existing savings of P1.865 billion to augment the P100 million budget for the Manila Hall of Justice, which is an item... in the 2012 budget of the Department of Justice-Office of the Secretary, which is within the Executive Department... (a) cross-border augmentation'

MR added that on March 5, 2013 (when Sereno was already CJ), Court issued resolution 'requested the DBM to transfer the (aforementioned sum of) P100 million in the budget of the DOJ for the Manila Hall of Justice to the Judiciary... to fund the construction of the Malabon Hall of Justice... which has no item in the 2012 or the 2013 GAA'

However, after petitions questioning DAP constitutionality had been filed and while being heard, CJ Sereno in letter dated 23 December 2013 informed DBM that SC was withdrawing its request to realign the P100 million

'These two instances show both cross-border transfers on the part of the Supreme Court -- (a) the augmentation of an item in the Executive from funds in the Judiciary; and, (b) the transfer of funds from the Executive to the Supreme Court, whether or not for purposes of augmentation'
Q8: In view of foregoing documented claims, is SC also guilty of performing unconstitutional 'acts and practices'?
OSG did NOT denounce these acts as unconstitutional

Merely observed that 'the Honorable Court's practices were based on an understanding of the constitutional provision that coincides with the government's... and validate the respondent's theory of benign and necessary interdepartmental augmentations'

Added that this 'practice of cross-border transfers was not begun by President Aquino, as in fact Presidents under the 1987 Constitutions -- Fidel V. Ramos, Joseph E. Estrada, and Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo -- have, from time to time, transferred savings to other branches of government'
Q9: As retired chief justice, please comment on these two 'acts and practices' of SC
OSG was careful not to denounce Court's alleged cross-border transfers and attempt to augment a non-existing budget item to fund construction of Malabon court house
Court said it will, in resolving MR, justify these two acts; CJP won't preempt such justification
However, in CJP's humble view, these two SC actions reinforce application of 'operative fact doctrine'
I.e., that acts and practices done pursuant to a law or executive issuance prior to declaration of their unconstitutionality are valid and enforceable as matter of equity and fairness

Also strengthen CJP's answer to Q3 last Sunday: 'alien' statement on page 90 of decision saying operative fact doctrine 'cannot apply to the authors, proponents and implementors of the DAP...' should be deleted from decision, or clarified to assure it is not prejudgment of liability, or explained that it is merely nonbinding obiter dictum (side comment) not supported by decision's fallo or dispositive portion
Finally, two acts affirm fact that power of augmentation is quite difficult to understand even by most astute legal minds
Not taught in law schools
Neither explained in standard political law textbooks
In view of controversy it has spawned, CJP sure it would henceforth be discoursed in classrooms, legal forums and new political law books

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban delivers the second installment of his DAP-decision Q&A, picking up where A405 (July 20) left off with questions Q6-Q9. Q6: In Question No. 5 a week ago, CJ said PNoy can use DAP again in the future provided he observes the constitutional limitations pointed out in the SC decision -- can the Senate president, House speaker, CJ, and heads of the independent constitutional commissions do the same? Yes, the same power of augmentation -- which was given the sophisticated name of DAP by PNoy -- is granted by the Constitution to the aforesaid officials; thus they may continue exercising such power (which to stress was not struck down as unconstitutional by the SC) provided they, like the President is required to, observe the limitations pointed out in the decision. In the past, the Constitutional and Fiscal Autonomy Group, composed of the judiciary, Office of the Ombudsman, Comelec, COA and CSC, routinely used the power of augmentation to realign savings from vacant positions to increase the compensation and fringe benefits of incumbent officials and personnel. Q7: please explain PNoy's claim, contained in the MR filed by the OSG, that the SC has committed two 'acts and practices' that did not observe the limitations set out in the decision. In its MR, the OSG said that on July 17, 2012, when Justice Antonio T. Carpio was the acting CJ (during the interregnum after CJ Renato C. Corona was ousted and disqualified from holding any public office by the Senate per its 'Judgment' dated May 28, 2012, and the appointment of new CJ Maria Lourdes P.A. Sereno on Aug 24, 2012), the Court 'earmarked its existing savings of P1.865 billion to augment the P100 million budget for the Manila Hall of Justice, which is an item... in the 2012 budget of the Department of Justice-Office of the Secretary, which is within the Executive Department... (a) cross-border augmentation.' The MR added that on March 5, 2013 (when Sereno was already CJ), the Court issued a resolution which 'requested the DBM to transfer the P100 million in the budget of the DOJ for the Manila Hall of Justice to the Judiciary... to fund the construction of the Malabon Hall of Justice... which has no item in the 2012 or the 2013 GAA.' However, after the petitions questioning the constitutionality of the DAP had been filed and while they were being heard, CJ Sereno, in a letter dated 23 December 2013, informed the DBM that the SC was withdrawing its request to realign the P100 million intended for the Manila Hall of Justice to the budget of the Judiciary. These two instances show both cross-border transfers on the part of the SC -- (a) the augmentation of an item in the Executive from funds in the Judiciary; and (b) the 'transfer' of funds from the Executive to the SC, whether or not for purposes of augmentation. Q8: in view of the foregoing documented claims, is the SC also guilty of performing unconstitutional 'acts and practices'? The OSG did not denounce these acts as unconstitutional; it merely observed that 'the Honorable Court's practice(s) were based on an understanding of the constitutional provision that coincides with the government's... and validate the respondent's theory of benign and necessary interdepartmental augmentations.' It added that this 'practice of cross-border transfers was not begun by PNoy, as in fact Presidents under the 1987 Constitutions -- Ramos, Estrada, and GMA -- have, from time to time, transferred savings to other branches of government.' Q9: as a retired CJ, please comment on these two 'acts and practices' of the SC. The OSG was careful not to denounce the Court's alleged cross-border transfers and attempt to augment a non-existing budget item to fund the construction of the Malabon court house; the Court said that, in resolving the MR, it will justify these two acts -- CJ will not preempt such justification now. However, in CJ's humble view, these two SC actions reinforce the application of the 'operative fact doctrine,' i.e., that acts and practices done pursuant to a law or executive issuance prior to the declaration of their unconstitutionality are valid and enforceable as a matter of equity and fairness. So also, they strengthen CJ's answer to Q3 last Sunday (A405): that the 'alien' statement on page 90 of the decision saying that the operative fact doctrine 'cannot apply to the authors, proponents and implementors of the DAP...' should be deleted from the decision, or clarified to assure that it is not a prejudgment of liability, or explained that it is merely a non-binding obiter dictum (side comment) not supported by the decision's fallo or dispositive portion. Finally, the two acts affirm the fact that the power of augmentation is quite difficult to understand even by the most astute legal minds -- in fact, it is not taught in law schools, neither is it explained in standard political law textbooks; however, in view of the controversy it has now spawned, CJ is sure it would henceforth be discoursed in classrooms, legal forums and new political law books.
